equipment_type: Kitchen hood demand ventilation status outputs (exhaust and make-up air fans)
applies_to: Virtual Output Modules of a Melink Intelli-Hood 4 system, which give a BMS extra status outputs over BACnet.
summary: A Virtual Output Module is a virtual BACnet IP device behind the Intelli-Hood System Controller with four read-only digital outputs. They work like the controller's relay outputs: each is given a function in the configuration (Fan On, Temperature Alarm, Smoke, System Fault, VFD Fault...) and the BMS reads its state.
notes: The PICS object table ticks the Analog Value column for these four objects, but their identifiers are BV 0-BV 3 and the states are binary; they are listed as BV here.
Output functions include Temperature Alarm, Smoke, Fan On, MUA Damper, Temperature Fault, Optic Fault, VFD Fault, System Fault, 24/7 and External Relay Reset.

source.title: Intelli-Hood BACnet Protocol Implementation Conformance Statement (PICS)

integration.summary: Assign each virtual output a function (for example Fan On and System Fault) and its hood groups in the Intelli-Hood configuration, then read the four BVs from the BMS.

setup: The System Controller is the main BACnet IP device (default Device ID 654000) and a virtual router (default DNET 654) for the fan, hood controller and virtual module devices; UDP port 47808.

With BACnet Auto Number on (default), the virtual devices are numbered from 654001: exhaust fans and auxiliary airflows (sorted by name), then hood controllers, virtual output modules, virtual input modules.
IP defaults to DHCP. BACnet runs on IPv4 or IPv6, not both; for IPv6 set IP Type to 'IPv4 & IPv6' and BACnet IP Type to IPv6 (multicast scope default ff05).
Settings are on the Touchpad (System Controller configuration) or the web configurator at http://<controller IP>/ih4-configurator.
Virtual Output Module Device IDs are shown on the Touchpad under Status > Virtual Output Modules.
gotchas: Front ends that send Who-Is without routing only find the System Controller; run a network/router discovery, select the router with the Intelli-Hood DNET, then discover devices again.
The DNET must be unique; another router or BBMD using 654 breaks access to the virtual devices.
